label: JZ Mock C · Paper 2 · Question 6
knowledgePattern: Audit a fractional-power derivative and its sign-preserving division
solution:
The power rule gives f′(x)=x4/3+x1/3−2x−2/3. Factoring yields x−2/3(x2+x−2). These are steps 1 and 2.

For every nonzero real x, x−2/3=1/(x3)2>0. Thus the condition f′(x)≥0 is equivalent to x2+x−2≥0, so steps 3 and 4 are valid.

Factoring as (x−1)(x+2)≥0 gives x≤−2 or x≥1. Both endpoints give zero gradient, and neither interval contains the excluded input zero. All the steps are correct. Answer G.

hints.title: Check the derivative first
hints.body: Differentiate each power in f(x) separately. Then multiply out the factorisation in line II to check it.
hints.recap: For a power, multiply by the exponent and reduce the exponent by one.
hints.pitfall: Negative and fractional powers use the same power rule on the stated domain.
hints.pause: Compare your result with lines I and II before moving on.

recall.reminder: For a power, multiply by the exponent and reduce the exponent by one.

hints.title: Write the fractional power as a root
hints.body: Write x−2/3 using x3 and a reciprocal. What sign does this expression have when x is negative? What about positive x?
hints.recap: The sign of a factor determines whether division reverses an inequality.
hints.pitfall: Zero is excluded in the question and must stay excluded.
hints.pause: Use this sign check for line IV, then verify the quadratic sign intervals in the remaining lines. Do not assume there must be an error.

recall.reminder: The sign of a factor determines whether division reverses an inequality.
